title: Translate customer commitment tiers into reserved-pool behavior and isolation controls
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem statement: Customers purchase monthly/annual committed capacity tiers but onboarding, upgrades, and real application traffic produce mismatches between contract language and runtime behavior. We need a clear, auditable translation layer that maps a customer's contractual commitment (tier, region, burst allowance, preemptibility) to concrete reserved-pool configuration, autoscale headroom, and isolation controls implemented by the Dedicated runtime and billing pipeline.
background: Sales & Finance frequently receive questions about what exactly a "tier" buys: how many GPUs, how much burst, whether preemptible nodes are allowed, and what HA guarantees apply. Engineering has many knobs (pool size, prewarm count, eviction policies, burst windows) but no canonical mapping from contract terms to runtime defaults. This creates onboarding delays, customer confusion, and manual operator work.
goals: 1) Define canonical mapping from commitment tiers to reserved-pool configs and default isolation settings. 2) Surface mapping in Console and API during onboarding and contract changes. 3) Ensure autoscale and burst policies respect contractual limits and generate telemetry for billing reconciliation. 4) Provide acceptance tests and rollout plan for both Hosted Dedicated and Private deployments.
non_goals: 1) Redesign pricing model. 2) Change SLA guarantees outside contract amendments. 3) Implement new hardware allocation algorithms (this ticket provides config mappings and UX only).
scope: IN: mapping table, Console UX changes for onboarding flow, API param additions for commitment translation, operator API for manual overrides, telemetry/billing events. OUT: wholesale pricing changes, multi-tenant scheduler redesign, on-prem packaging changes beyond config schema.
out_of_scope: Contract negotiation process and legal approval flow (we will emit clear artifacts for legal but not change contracts).
proposed_solution: Create a 'Commitment Translation' microservice (logical, can be part of existing capacity service) that:
proposed_solution_details: - Takes Contract/Tier metadata and outputs a reserved-pool spec (pool_size, prewarm_count, burst_window_seconds, soft_isolation_class, preemptible_allowed). - Exposes an idempotent API used by Console onboarding, customer-ops, and the runtime controller. - Emits audit events for billing and change management. - Provides a Console preview UI showing resulting runtime configuration before activation. - Implements validation and safe defaults for upgrades and downgrades (e.g., downgrade cannot drop below active allocated pods without operator confirmation).
autoscale_interplay: Define clear rules for autoscale: autoscale may expand capacity for transient bursts only up to 'burst_window' and only if account has BurstAllowance > 0. Autoscale scale-down must respect contract minimums. All autoscale decisions should be labeled with reason codes for billing (e.g., 'burst:overcommit', 'prewarm:scheduled').
isolation_controls: Translate contractual isolation into enforcement knobs: 'strong' -> strict tenant fencing, no shared worker placement; 'soft' -> prefer dedicated placement but allow co-loc with low-noise tenants; 'none' -> shared placement allowed. Include operator override API with audit log. Ensure Console clearly displays the active isolation enforcement level and any deviation from the committed level.
billing_and_telemetry: Emit structured telemetry events mapping runtime usage to commitment buckets: reserved_usage, burst_usage, preemptible_usage. Provide a reconciliation report for Finance (CSV export) showing hour-by-hour attribution to contract vs burst. Add metric tags: commit_tier, pool_id, translation_version.
console_changes: - Onboarding wizard: present a preview of derived runtime config and highlight any manual steps required (e.g., network ranges for Private). - Active subscription page: show live pool status, headroom, burst consumption, and next recommended action. - Operator page: allow safe reduce/increase with warnings and required approvals.
api_changes: Add POST /commitments/translate and GET /commitments/:id/derived-config. API returns a stable config_id that can be applied to runtime. All API responses include 'translation_version' and 'audit_token'.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sample contract, POST /commitments/translate returns a derived config that matches the mapping table (unit tests covering 8 representative tiers)
Console onboarding shows a preview and requires explicit confirmation before applying a downgrade that would evict active allocations
Autoscale decisions during a synthetic load test annotate events with reason codes and do not exceed burst allowance beyond window seconds
Telemetry pipeline emits 'reserved_usage' and 'burst_usage' for each hour and Finance reconciliation CSV matches expected consumption in integration test
Operator override flow requires two-step confirmation and writes to audit log visible in Console
success_metrics: Reduce average onboarding time for Dedicated customers from 5 business days to 2 business days
Decrease number of manual_OPS interventions for mapping issues to < 2 per month
Billing reconciliation mismatches due to translation errors < 0.5% of committed spend within first 90 days
rollout_plan: 1) Implement translation logic behind feature flag and unit tests (eng sprint 1)
2) Console preview + API + integration test in staging (eng sprint 2)
3) Beta with 3 pilot customers; monitor telemetry & billing reconciliation (2 weeks)
4) Open rollout to all new commits; migrate existing customers opt-in over 60 days
5) Full defaulting for all new contracts in release dedicated-2026.04
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Downgrade triggers eviction of live allocations -> Mitigation: require operator approval and soft-deferred step-down with customer notification
Risk: Translation versioning mismatch between Console and runtime -> Mitigation: include translation_version in all applied configs and refuse apply if runtime is incompatible
Risk: Over-attributing burst to reserved buckets causing billing disputes -> Mitigation: conservative defaulting and explicit reconciliation reports exposed to customers
open_questions: Should we allow customers to opt out of automatic prewarm for specific deployments?
What escalation path do Sales teams use if a customer disputes a translation mapping?
How do we model hybrid commits that span multiple regions with different instance families?
